title: Park repositories instead of disposing them
summary: Switching repositories threw the old one's data away, so going back read everything again. The engine now keeps every repository it has seen.

slides.title: What changes
slides.lede: Switching repositories parks the old one instead of disposing it, so going back to it shows its data at once.
slides.body:
1. The service keeps a handle per repository and selects one
2. Parked reads serve what they hold
3. Parking stops discovery and drops diff patches, nothing else
4. Writes refuse a parked repository
5. The pull request list keeps every scope on show

slides.title: Many handles, one selected
slides.lede: `open()` moves the selection and parks the handle before it; `get()` hands out a parked handle without selecting it.

before.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  O["open(B)"] --> S[repository service]
  S --> B["B: current"]
  S -.->|dispose| A["A: gone"]
before.caption: Before: one handle at a time

after.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  O["open(B)"] --> S[repository service]
  G["get(C)"] --> S
  S --> B["B: selected"]
  S --> A["A: parked"]
  S --> C["C: parked"]
after.caption: After: every handle stays

slides.title: Parked reads answer from what they hold
slides.lede: A parked repository serves held data at once and refreshes behind it only after an hour; with nothing held, it reads and waits.
slides.body: The selected repository keeps each resource's own TTL. A failed background refresh does not fail the answer; the error stays in the snapshot.

slides.title: Parking lets go of two things
slides.lede: A parked repository stops session discovery and drops its diff patches; everything else stays, and no handle is ever disposed.
slides.body: Patches go because each can be 64 MiB and re-reading one is a local Git read. The live checkout diff keeps its one-second TTL: agents keep editing a parked repository.

slides.title: Only the selected repository takes writes
slides.lede: Reads answer any repository; every write checks the handle is selected before it starts, and review writes check again before calling the provider.
slides.body: Review writes use `selected()` and `assertWritable()`; worktree and config writes use `assertSelected()`.

slides.title: The pull request list keeps every scope on show
slides.lede: The list never evicts a scope a repository shows; past its bound it drops only scopes a config change left behind.
slides.body: `refreshInBackground(cwd, { maxAge })` lets `prewarm()` skip the read while a parked list is under an hour old.

slides.title: Look closely: get() writes config
slides.lede: Creating a handle runs `autoDetectProjectConfig`, which writes the project config, so `get()` writes for a repository nobody selected.
slides.body: This sits outside the rule that parked handles refuse writes.

slides.title: Look closely: memory and edges
slides.lede: Handles, their subscriptions and every shown pull request scope live as long as the process; that is by design and is unbounded.
slides.body:
- `serveParked` returns data without its error, so callers see stale data instead of a failure
- `mentions` is a read, but refused while parked
- Worktree commands check selection only before their first await
- Not checked: a real cross-repository switch in the desktop. No draft comments.
